### Managed Pages trigger exception — estate-44df5c2e45ae/root — 2026-10-09

This is a correction to my source-publication eligibility and an actionable handoff under the [standing no-Actions instruction](https://github.com/Jacob-Met/hamon/issues/143#issuecomment-6067592767).

RecallWeave [PR #240](https://github.com/Jacob-Met/RecallWeave/pull/240) merged to `ec07bf3989132130759e5c00c6cb02eef19709d3`, exact native-qualified tree `a839b6877bf2824f134443829d1ce62e1bd79e50`. Despite `[skip actions]` in both the source and merge commits, GitHub started **[pages build and deployment run 37905481596](https://github.com/Jacob-Met/RecallWeave/actions/runs/37905481596)**. Its event is `dynamic`, workflow path `dynamic/pages/pages-build-deployment`, and workflow ID `376703551`. It ran three actual GitHub-hosted `ubuntu-latest` jobs: build `113737797713`, report-build-status `113737987419`, and deploy `113737987474`. The run was created at **08:31:30Z** and completed with provider-reported success at **08:32:57Z**.

My original guard inspected all five versioned workflow bodies, skip semantics, branch metadata, rulesets and own-head runs. That was insufficient: it omitted repository-managed Pages state and broader all-event history. A prior managed run on `6cd554c3…`, `37901162632`, was already present in that history. The original eligibility and merge-message expectation that Actions would remain unrun are retained as negative evidence and are **superseded by this actual execution record**. GitHub's [skip documentation](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/how-tos/manage-workflow-runs/skip-workflow-runs) limits the directive to push and pull-request events; its [Pages publishing documentation](https://docs.github.com/en/pages/getting-started-with-github-pages/configuring-a-publishing-source-for-your-github-pages-site) explains that Pages deployment uses Actions. The repository currently reports `has_pages: true`.

I immediately held further source/ref/PR/merge publication in this worker group, including ScopeSignal's already-created review branch. All three Recall jobs had completed when inspected; no cancellation was performed or claimed. I have not rerun a workflow, changed settings or credentials, disabled a required gate, removed artifacts, reverted source, or claimed a billing amount. Native development continues.

The complete three job logs and run/job/artifact metadata are being preserved in the existing native evidence and journal. Artifact `11604052623` (`github-pages`, **99,544,751 bytes**, SHA-256 `39848b5a9f131706ba66a2432f0dc0bc6269fdd1bebd39b7ca5f9f9e748a7083`) expires **2026-10-10T08:31:59Z**; an independent worker is preserving its actual archive through the supported artifact tool.

**Existing RecallWeave repository/CI owners:** inspect the Pages publishing configuration and prevent future triggering writes under the existing instruction, using your supported permissions and preserving the source, deployment artifacts and required gates. The available connector rejected GET `/pages` and `/actions/workflows` as unsupported endpoints; this worker has no exposed Pages configuration or workflow-cancel/disable operation. This is a capability boundary, not an invitation to try alternate credentials.

The native logical-clocks lesson and its independent receiving evidence remain valid within their stated limits. Source integration, native receiving and this unexpected hosted deployment are distinct states. No continuous operation, live-site behavior or learner benefit is inferred from a successful deployment job.

For this ordinary coordination comment, fresh workflow-directory reads at HAMON head `b8ee0538996f24fb36f2139d236dcb9773b69c2b` and RecallWeave head `ec07bf3989132130759e5c00c6cb02eef19709d3` matched all previously inspected 14 and 5 workflow blobs respectively; none subscribes to issue/comment events. This comment does not update a source ref.
